### eafbeeda11db9915df5d05c319ff3c5bb6a44b6d

[eafbeeda11db9915df5d05c319ff3c5bb6a44b6d](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/eafbeeda11db9915df5d05c319ff3c5bb6a44b6d)

Date: 2026-08-29T21:34:05-03:00 · Classification: Other Changes (unknown) · Systems: Combat, Extraction, Inventory & Loot, Art & Animation, Build & Tooling, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
Integrate modular armor sets and update combat visuals
```

#### Original body

```text
- Replace placeholder armor assets with the ArcaneMage definitions while preserving their legacy IDs and GUIDs.
- Add ArmyRanger and HeavyArmor equipment definitions with complete Idle and Walk sprite mappings for all six directions.
- Register all twelve armor pieces in the deterministic loot catalog and productive container loot table.
- Separate the 16-stack inventory capacity from the catalog index representation limit, allowing the 22-definition catalog.
- Keep equipped armor above its corresponding base sprite throughout animation.
- Make equipped gloves replace the base hand sprites to prevent exposed skin pixels.
- Add integrity tests for armor definitions, slots, catalog positions, sprite mappings, both hands, loot availability and expanded catalog support.
- Replace the obsolete ArrowProjectile prefab with MagicProjectile and update the DartProjectile sprite.
- Move the ExtractionSanctuary visual behind gameplay entities.
- Remove obsolete placeholder tests, assets and orphaned metadata.
```

### a34afeefc9cf6d87742821307cb80ef50b91d4ac

[a34afeefc9cf6d87742821307cb80ef50b91d4ac](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/a34afeefc9cf6d87742821307cb80ef50b91d4ac)

Date: 2026-08-29T03:04:35-03:00 · Classification: Architecture & Infrastructure (inferred) · Systems: Art & Animation

Flags: secondary

#### Original subject

```text
Configure and slice character set sprite sheets
```

#### Original body

```text
Configure the ArcaneMage, ArmyRanger, and HeavyArmor sprite sheets to match the base character import settings.

- Set all sheets to Multiple sprite mode at 16 PPU
- Enable Point filtering, Clamp wrapping, and alpha transparency
- Disable compression and mipmaps
- Slice Idle sheets into six 96x96 frames
- Slice Walk sheets into eight 96x96 frames
- Preserve the original PNG files, GUIDs, sprite IDs, names, and folder structure
```

### 7def33564a1afef1566f19a35a7b49a7e1300f7b

[7def33564a1afef1566f19a35a7b49a7e1300f7b](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/7def33564a1afef1566f19a35a7b49a7e1300f7b)

Date: 2026-08-28T21:10:46-03:00 · Classification: Bug Fixes (explicit) · Systems: Combat, Movement, Documentation

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
fix(combat): aim ranged enemy attacks at the target's current position
```

#### Original body

```text
fix(combat): aim ranged enemy attacks at the target's current position

Ranged enemies fired every projectile toward a stale direction once the
player entered attack range.

Two defects compounded:

- EnemyMovementAIController gated the FacingDirection write behind
  canMove. EnemyAttackState disables control to hold the enemy still,
  so facing stopped updating entirely on entering Attack.
- EnemyCombatAIController passed that frozen FacingDirection into
  TryCommitAttack. FacingDirection derives from the pursuit path and can
  point around an obstacle, so it is not a valid aim source even when it
  does update.

Facing now resolves toward the target's current position while movement
is disabled, keeping the enemy stationary but tracking. Ranged aim is
computed per attack from _attackOrigin to the target. Melee keeps
consuming FacingDirection, so its arc is unchanged. The direction is
frozen into the pending AttackRequest at commit time, so a projectile
keeps the direction it was fired with and never homes.

Reuses the existing PlayerAimMath.TryResolveDirection helper instead of
adding new direction math. Documents the facing/aim boundary in
EnemyCombatArchitecture.md.
```

#### Changed paths

```text
Project Grimhold/Assets/Scripts/Player/Movement/EnemyMovementAIController.cs

```

```text
- spriteMeshType Full Rect + point filter on all directions.

- Death sheet: auto-slice had split frame 1 into two sprites (7 total);

  (stop time 0.5833 -> 0.5).
```

### 2e40e65ae02f654e84e9325c69025d1f4ee1b81b

[2e40e65ae02f654e84e9325c69025d1f4ee1b81b](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/2e40e65ae02f654e84e9325c69025d1f4ee1b81b)

Date: 2026-08-28T19:43:24-03:00 · Classification: Bug Fixes (explicit) · Systems: Extraction, Networking & Sessions, UI, Art & Animation, Build & Tooling, Documentation, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
fix(networking): return the Host to Town after Cancel Raid
```

#### Original body

```text
Cancel Raid aborted every participant with return authorization, including the
operational Host's. RaidMenuPresenter observed IsReturnAuthorized without
distinguishing roles and called ReturnParticipantToTownAsync(), which
SessionConnectionCoordinator correctly rejects for an operational Host with
InvalidRequest, leaving the return latch set, the menu closed and the Host stuck
in Gameplay with a live runner.

A cancelled Host participant ends as Aborted with FinalizationCause.None, so it is
not an accepted terminal result and RaidResultsReturnPolicy cannot authorize its
Results return. That gate stays unchanged; the cancellation return gets its own
explicit entry point into the existing pending-Host-return lifecycle.

- RaidMenuPresenter: gate the individual participant return behind
  ShouldStartParticipantReturn, which requires a resolved non-Host operational
  role, so an unresolved role during shutdown starts nothing. The operational Host
  only acknowledges the closure locally, once, when its participant is authorized.
- RaidMenuPresenter: inspect the SessionTransitionResult of the participant return
  and release the latch, restoring the menu, on any non-Succeeded result instead of
  leaving the UI silently closed. Exceptions remain a separate failure path.
- SessionConnectionCoordinator: arm the existing pending host-return latch once when
  an authoritative HostCancellation closure is observed. ObservePendingHostResultsReturn
  still starts the single global ReturnToTownAsync() only at MatchPhase.Finished with
  no Raiding participants and no connected remote peers, so the Host keeps the
  authoritative runner while Clients remain.
- Document the two valid entry points of the pending operational-Host return in
  LobbyAndSessionTransitionArchitecture.md.

Clients keep their existing individual participant return. Host Migration is
unaffected: only RaidClosureReason.HostCancellation arms this path.

EditMode: 961/978 passed; the 17 failures are pre-existing prefab, animation and
loot asset checks unrelated to this change. The touched fixtures pass 113/113.
Solo-Host and two-application Host+Client cancellation still require manual Unity
validation.
```

#### Original subject

```text
feat(progression): add raid loot provenance and eligibility
```

#### Original body

```text
- Add raid-scoped participant and team identities for loot ownership tracking.
- Track original loot provenance as Dungeon or Player(RaidParticipantId).
- Preserve provenance across inventory, equipment, containers, pickups, world drops and corpses.
- Add typed raid launch participants with initial team affiliation.
- Add immutable affiliation snapshots derived from the raid participant assignment.
- Add pure loot eligibility resolution for Dungeon, own, teammate and enemy origins.
- Preserve eligibility rules independently of loot transfers and current ownership.
- Formalize raid loot endpoint capacity to 16 distinct loot types.
- Add validation for mixed-origin stacks, transfers, equipment and corpse flows.
- Update progression, loot and session architecture documentation.
- Add focused EditMode and PlayMode coverage for provenance and eligibility.
- Leave loot Value, extraction XP calculation and persistent progression integration for the next task.
```

#### Original subject

```text
Fix weapon grip tracking and sorting layers
```

#### Original body

```text
Align weapon visual entirely to the character's animated right hand by injecting RightHandGrip position curves into all 12 Player locomotion animations. Replace hardcoded swing offsets with dynamic tracking, ensuring the weapon matches the grip point without overriding body presentation. Increase rendering sorting order for the hand and gloves to strictly wrap the weapon, and expose a configurable SwingArc parameter in WeaponDefinition for live procedural swing adjustments.
```

### d5e59353647c4486611291e7d7cabd27cd218e90

[d5e59353647c4486611291e7d7cabd27cd218e90](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/d5e59353647c4486611291e7d7cabd27cd218e90)

Date: 2026-08-23T23:01:08-03:00 · Classification: Features (inferred) · Systems: Combat, Art & Animation, Build & Tooling, Documentation

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
Add explicit 2-stage procedural melee swing presentation
```

#### Original body

```text
- Introduce _swingStartAngle (60) and _swingFollowThroughAngle (-30) to PlayerWeaponPresenter for a sweep animation that crosses the weapon's resting direction.
- Refactor the swing logic to interpolate in two stages: 70% sweep and 30% recovery to neutral pose.
- Remove hardcoded mirror math based on facing.x and instead use explicit _swingSign configured via WeaponDirectionPreset.
- Set explicit swing signs in NetworkPlayer.prefab for all 6 directions, verifying N and S sweep outward from the side where the right hand visually rests.
- Maintain PlayerWeaponPresenter as the exclusive owner of the presentation and use the existing AttackPerformed event without altering combat logic or networking.
```

### 2913e27acb6c07f1e223c06c6f865f7d495c0a12

[2913e27acb6c07f1e223c06c6f865f7d495c0a12](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/2913e27acb6c07f1e223c06c6f865f7d495c0a12)

Date: 2026-08-20T19:15:46-03:00 · Classification: Other Changes (unknown) · Systems: Combat, Extraction, Inventory & Loot, Networking & Sessions, UI, Persistence & Backend, Build & Tooling, Documentation, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
Unify the Stash screen with the Raid inventory and prepare Equipment in Town
```

#### Original body

```text
The Stash screen was a fork of the Raid inventory that stopped matching it when
the Raid UI moved into the prefab: it still instantiated slots at runtime, kept
two dead RaidLootPanelView components wired to a removed _slotPrefab field, and
floated its two prepared weapon slots over the loadout panel with hardcoded
anchored positions. Town preparation also covered weapons only, so the armor
introduced by the six-slot Equipment work could not be prepared before a raid.

Stash screen composition
- LobbyStashUI stops creating UI. It binds two authored RaidLootPanelView panels,
  six authored RaidInventorySlotView Equipment views, both bulk buttons and the
  context menu, and pads each received stack list with empty entries up to its
  authored pool exactly as RaidInventoryProjection does for the Raid screen.
  Content beyond the pool is reported once and the panel shows its existing
  "Lleno" feedback instead of silently dropping stacks.
- Both panels are TransferWithContextMenu, so a stack can be equipped from the
  Stash or from the Loadout. The menu offers only the slots EquipmentSlotRules
  reports as compatible, resolved from the category now carried by
  RaidInventorySlotData, so the view needs no catalog of its own. A left click on
  an occupied Equipment slot releases that exact slot.
- TownStashView becomes an authored component that only shows and hides the
  screen; TownStashPresenter resolves it instead of adding components and the
  Canvas sorting order is authored in the prefab. The development-only [StashUI]
  traces are gone; the dependency warnings stay.
- StashInventory.prefab now holds the panels, both 16-slot pools, the equipment
  panel and the screen root. The prefab is the only source of truth for that
  layout: the temporary authoring tools that seeded both inventory screens are
  removed, so nothing can regenerate the hierarchy, renumber the authored slots
  or overwrite manual layout work. Adding a slot means adding it in the prefab
  and appending it to the panel's _authoredSlots.

Town Equipment preparation
- PreparedWeaponLoadout becomes PreparedEquipmentLoadout, covering the six slots
  of EquipmentSlot. EquipmentSlotRules owns the canonical slot order and decides
  compatibility; weapon slots additionally require a usable WeaponDefinition, and
  one identity used by several slots requires one owned unit per reference.
- LocalProfileStore exposes TryAssignPreparedEquipment/TryClearPreparedEquipment.
  Prepared units must belong to the Loadout because that is what the reservation
  transfers, so equipping a unit that still lives in the Stash pulls the missing
  units into the Loadout inside the same atomic commit; a rejected assignment
  moves nothing and a full Loadout rejects the pull. Releasing a slot leaves the
  unit in the Loadout. Reconciliation releases the last slots first.
- The recovery weapon guarantee and the Slot 2 to Slot 1 normalization no longer
  overwrite prepared armor: armor is optional, never granted and never rewritten.
- The profile codec gains four additive armor fields for the profile and for the
  reservation. CurrentSchemaVersion stays 1 on purpose: the fields are optional,
  so a profile saved before them decodes with empty armor, while bumping the
  version would reject every existing local profile as UnsupportedVersion.
- RaidAdmissionData carries one reference per Equipment slot in
  EquipmentSlotRules.AllSlots order, RaidLoadoutRules validates range, the
  mandatory weapon and reference multiplicity, and the admission token moves to
  canonical version 6 with four extra bytes, still inside its 512-byte bound.
- TryInitializePreparedEquipment equips the six slots on spawn and rechecks slot
  compatibility against the catalog before extracting any unit, so a reference
  that no longer fits its slot rejects the admission instead of dropping the
  piece. FusionSessionLauncher verifies all six slots before confirming.

Design alignment
04 - Character Build Design puts armor inside the prepared build and allows
changing it in Town, and keeps one valid weapon as the only launch requirement.
02 - Estados del Juego enables Inventory, Equipment and Stash during Expedition
Preparation. Armor still carries no stats, as documented in PlayerCombat.

Verification
- Assembly-CSharp and Assembly-CSharp-Editor compile with 0 errors; the remaining
  warnings are pre-existing.
- The full EditMode suite was run after the Stash unification only: 706/720, with
  the same 14 pre-existing failures as the previous commit. It has NOT been run
  again after the Equipment preparation change, which updates existing tests and
  adds PreparedEquipmentTests.
- Manual: the Stash screen was opened in the Editor after authoring and presents
  the six Equipment slots and both panels correctly. A complete Town to Raid cycle
  carrying prepared armor, and Host/Client admission, remain manually unverified.
```

### ec022c752ca2b2a63cd97ed81808bd57b4b2ab93

[ec022c752ca2b2a63cd97ed81808bd57b4b2ab93](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/ec022c752ca2b2a63cd97ed81808bd57b4b2ab93)

Date: 2026-08-20T17:36:05-03:00 · Classification: Features (inferred) · Systems: Combat, Extraction, Inventory & Loot, Networking & Sessions, UI, Art & Animation, Build & Tooling, Documentation, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
Add six-slot player Equipment and move raid inventory UI into the prefab
```

#### Original body

```text
Equipment stops being "the weapon system" and becomes the single authoritative
source of what the player has equipped, covering the six MVP slots defined by
Character Build: two weapon quick slots plus Helmet, Armor, Gloves and Boots.

Slot contracts (Assets/Scripts/Player/Equipment/)
- EquipmentSlot enumerates exactly the six slots; the two weapon values match
  WeaponSlot so the value already replicated by the active-weapon selection and
  carried by the equipment RPC keeps its meaning.
- EquipmentSlotRules is the single source of truth for compatibility. Loot only
  classifies a unit through LootCategory (extended with Helmet/Armor/Gloves/
  Boots, preserving existing serialized values); deciding which slot may receive
  it belongs to Equipment. No ArmorDefinition and no armor stats were added.
- WeaponEquipResult becomes EquipmentOperationResult with explicit numeric
  values, since results travel through the RPC as ints. Value 5 stays reserved
  by the removed WeaponAlreadyEquipped result. Armor operations no longer report
  weapon-flavoured errors.

Authoritative state
- PlayerWeaponEquipmentNetworkController is evolved rather than rewritten or
  renamed. Four networked catalog-index properties join the existing weapon
  slots; the replicated shape is otherwise untouched, so Host Migration keeps
  restoring through the same [Networked] mechanism with no new logic.
- Dependency validation is split: every equip/unequip needs only catalog,
  receiver and character, while the combat strategies are validated solely on
  the weapon branch. Equipping a helmet no longer depends on the projectile
  spawner.
- Armor never calls TryConfigureStrategy, TrySetActiveAttack or
  TryClearActiveAttack, and never enters the weapon-state comparison (renamed
  HasReplicatedWeaponStateChanged), so it cannot rebuild the active attack or
  disturb the authoritative cooldown. EquipmentRevision advances for all six
  slots. Rejected operations mutate neither Inventory nor Equipment.

Expedition ownership
- PlayerExpeditionLootSnapshot captures the six slots as named properties, not a
  positional array, and aggregates them into Combined. Equipped armor is now
  expedition property: lost on defeat and kept on extraction like a weapon.

Raid inventory UI
- No player UI component is created at runtime any more. RaidInventoryView
  exposes one named serialized field per equipment slot and RaidLootPanelView
  drives a serialized slot pool, showing the first N and hiding the rest instead
  of instantiating and destroying views.
- The Editor tool Grimhold/UI/Rebuild Raid Inventory UI authors the equipment
  panel and the three slot pools into NetworkPlayer.prefab through PrefabUtility,
  so the hierarchy stays fully editable in the Inspector.

Placeholder content
- Four placeholder armor definitions reuse the existing character body-part
  sprites so every slot can be exercised before real art exists. They are sold
  by the merchant and present in the container loot table. Town armor
  preparation is not implemented by this task; PreparedWeaponLoadout stays
  weapon-only.

Verification
- EditMode 706/720; the 14 failures are pre-existing (missing enemy prefabs and
  slime clip, SocialPlayer composition, Coins/Bone sell values).
- The 51 new EditMode equipment tests and the 9 new PlayMode tests all pass.
- PlayMode compared against a clean HEAD baseline: 84 failures before, 83 after,
  with no new failures introduced.
```

### 0023b0beee13af48746d1a36d8fb2ad7b2485c2d

[0023b0beee13af48746d1a36d8fb2ad7b2485c2d](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/0023b0beee13af48746d1a36d8fb2ad7b2485c2d)

Date: 2026-08-19T16:21:02-03:00 · Classification: Other Changes (unknown) · Systems: Combat, Inventory & Loot, Networking & Sessions, UI, Persistence & Backend, Input, Build & Tooling, Documentation, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
Complete two-slot weapon equipment and expedition preparation
```

#### Original body

```text
Extend Weapon Equipment to two authoritative quick slots and carry them across the
Town-Raid boundary. Prepared Weapon Slot 1 and Slot 2 are non-owning references over units
that remain in the Town Loadout; they enter the raid inside PendingLoadoutReservation, travel
as compact one-based references into ReservedLoadout in the version 5 admission token, and are
materialized by State Authority into replicated Equipment without duplicating inventory
ownership. Add the Town assignment UI over the Loadout context menu, raid inventory weapon
slots, weapon selection input, and the corresponding persistence, codec and admission coverage.

Introduce an expedition preparation boundary that runs before the reservation so requiring a
valid equipped weapon can no longer make Start Raid inert. TryPrepareExpeditionWeapons is
atomic, deterministic and idempotent: it leaves a valid Slot 1 untouched, normalizes the
effective selection when only Slot 2 is occupied, grants exactly one configured recovery weapon
when nothing is prepared while reusing an owned unit first, and fails explicitly on a persisted
reference that no longer resolves instead of overwriting it. Add the recovery_sword definition
with its own weapon definition, excluded from loot tables and without economic value, and
configure it as the Town recovery policy. TryCreateLoadoutReservation keeps requiring a valid
prepared weapon as a domain invariant, and Raid never grants recovery.

Stop a rejected local preparation from deadlocking the shared Town preparation.
TryStoreRaidLaunchContext now returns RaidLaunchPreparationResult so a transient retry is
distinguishable from a permanent rejection; a peer that cannot prepare reports it once per
launch revision instead of sending a false acknowledgement or waiting silently, and the State
Authority remains the only canceller. Arm a deadline for the acknowledgement phase so a launch
revision cannot wait indefinitely for a missing acknowledgement, and surface the rejection
reason through the existing Town feedback channel.

Fix two crashes in the new equipment surface. Every read-only query is guarded behind the
spawn check so presentation components that run their lifecycle callbacks during prefab
instantiation report no equipment rather than throwing on networked state, and the equipment
request RPC validates its byte-backed kind by range because Enum.IsDefined rejects the boxed
int outright.
```

### 82e47bc9480d27e5ff70e6518a576b58b9f23123

[82e47bc9480d27e5ff70e6518a576b58b9f23123](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/82e47bc9480d27e5ff70e6518a576b58b9f23123)

Date: 2026-08-18T20:05:34-03:00 · Classification: Features (inferred) · Systems: Combat, Movement, UI, Build & Tooling, Documentation, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
implement core game feel systems (screen shake, knockback, reactive aggro)
```

#### Original body

```text
Introduces three major game feel and feedback mechanics into the combat system to improve impact satisfaction and AI responsiveness:

1. Camera Screen Shake
- Implemented a trauma-based perlin noise camera shake system.
- Triggered on the local client via `LocalPlayerCameraShakeBinder` when receiving damage or confirming a valid hit against an enemy. Breakables are excluded.
- Controlled via `CameraShakeConfig` asset.

2. Physics-respecting Knockback
- Added configurable `KnockbackForce` to all `AttackConfig` assets.
- Both players and enemies receive an instantaneous impulse (`KnockbackVelocity`) that gracefully decays over time via friction.
- The displacement is fully resolved against world geometry by the `Kinematic2DMovementMotor`.

3. Reactive Targeting (Aggro)
- Enemies now instantly acquire the player as a target when hit by an attack, even from outside their normal line of sight or disengage range.
- Bypasses standard LOS checks for a configurable duration (`_aggroAlertDuration`) to ensure the enemy actively pursues the attacker.

Architecture:
- Added `IKnockbackMotor` and `IKnockbackReceiver` for universal knockback application without coupling DamageResolver to movement implementations.
- Added `IAggroReceiver` to `EnemyMovementAIController` to handle alert states.
- Extended `EntityRegistry` to safely resolve transforms, player identity, and feedback sinks during damage resolution.
```

```text
Data Models & Networking:

- Simplified PlayerJoinData to process only ProfileId encoded in strict UTF-8 (1-64 bytes).

- Reduced RaidAdmissionData variables and logic, fully stripping out class assignments.

Session Lifecycles & Coordination:

- Removed class-related dependencies from SessionConnectionCoordinator and launchers.

- Network Spawning directly references NetworkPlayer.prefab bypassing catalog lookups.

Presentation & Prefabs:

- Cleaned up MainMenu Canvas and MainMenuController.

- Stripped class-specific text bindings from RaidHudPresenter and NetworkPlayer.prefab.
```

### 52ec0020240c8be92b27b6b54372a746cd5bfd84

[52ec0020240c8be92b27b6b54372a746cd5bfd84](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/52ec0020240c8be92b27b6b54372a746cd5bfd84)

Date: 2026-08-12T01:07:54-03:00 · Classification: Features (inferred) · Systems: Networking & Sessions, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
implement stateful network orchestrator and duplicate-safe master client rules for shop
```

#### Original body

```text
Implements Stage 3 of US-16.

Introduces a robust idempotency protocol to handle network retries without double-execution:
- Created MerchantRequestValidator running on the Master Client to deduplicate incoming RPCs by maintaining a log of (PlayerRef, sequence) -> ShopTransactionId.
- Created MerchantTransactionOrchestrator on the requesting client to assign sequences, drop duplicate network responses, resolve prices locally against the LootDefinitionCatalog, and enforce atomic writes via LocalProfileStore.
- Decoupled interactable endpoints (TownMerchantNpcInteractable) from network logic (TownMerchantNetworkController).
- Removed declaredPrice from network payloads completely, cementing a Client-trusted / Local-authoritative economy model.
- Added 14 EditMode tests covering protocol collisions, replay scenarios, and lost responses.
```


#### Original body

```text
Implements Stage 2 of US-16.

Introduces atomic and deterministic purchase and sale primitives to LocalProfileStore.
Incorporates a Timestamp + Guid composite struct (ShopTransactionId) alongside a ShopIdempotencyWatermark in the local snapshot.
This eliminates long-term replay vulnerabilities when pruning transaction history beyond the 256 item limit.

- Exposes functionality through IShopTransactionService.
- Injects LocalShopTransactionService via the existing bootstrapper.
- Includes comprehensive EditMode testing (14 cases) validating success, failures, idempotency and correct watermark bounding.
```

```text
- Refactor PlayerWeaponPresentationMath to remove obsolete orbit/sorting methods.
```

```text
optimizar y hacer determinista la detección de objetivos && implementar sistema de patrullaje con waypoints
```

#### Original body

```text
- Reescribe EnemyMovementAIController separando lógica de sensores de FSM.
- Elimina FindObjectsByType y Random.Range de FixedUpdateNetwork.
- Introduce OverlapCircleNonAlloc determinista con ScanTimer (0.1s default) usando buffer pre-alocado.
- Separa _detectionRange y _disengageRange; añade _pursuitLostGraceTicks (10 ticks) para evitar flickering de borde.
- Añade _playerLayer y selección determinista (menor distancia + desempate por EntityId.Value).

- Añade componente de datos EnemyPatrolRoute con soporte para rutas circulares.
- Añade EnemyPatrolState al FSM e inyecta soporte en EnemyMovementAIController.
- Las transiciones desde Idle/Chase/Attack ahora vuelven a Patrol si hay ruta.
- Implementa ComputePatrolDirection con PatrolWaypointIndex [Networked].
- Evita 1-tick stop recalculando la dirección hacia el siguiente waypoint de inmediato.
```

### 36d776cdde279b5331649723cdca5a7abe4ae93f

[36d776cdde279b5331649723cdca5a7abe4ae93f](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/36d776cdde279b5331649723cdca5a7abe4ae93f)

Date: 2026-08-12T21:32:02-03:00 · Classification: Refactoring (inferred) · Systems: Extraction, Inventory & Loot, Networking & Sessions, UI, Build & Tooling, Documentation, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
Refactor host migration to recovery roster flow
```

#### Original body

```text
Reworked host migration into a recovery-only, multi-client lifecycle with explicit replacement roles (RecoveredAsHost vs RecoveredAsClient), local time budgets, and launcher adoption gates. Recovery now uses durable ProfileId-based roster tracking/sealing in NetworkSpawnManager, including early reconnect handling, authority rebind validation, and terminalization of unrecovered participants while preserving defeated corpse loot behavior. Also removed voluntary host-departure migration paths, switched role checks to operational host semantics, added restore guards for stateful scene objects, and updated architecture docs and migration-focused tests.
```

### 5cbb2bded5a2835d3810149764cb5de70d2d9267

[5cbb2bded5a2835d3810149764cb5de70d2d9267](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/5cbb2bded5a2835d3810149764cb5de70d2d9267)

Date: 2026-08-12T17:20:41-03:00 · Classification: Features (inferred) · Systems: Extraction, Inventory & Loot, Networking & Sessions, UI, Build & Tooling, Documentation, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
Add defeated spectator flow and return gating
```

#### Original body

```text
Implements a full defeated-player spectator lifecycle with role-aware return behavior. Defeated clients now require a one-shot controlled-return authorization keyed by ProfileId + RaidGenerationId, while defeated hosts are explicitly blocked from returning during an active raid.

Adds ControlledReturnKey/ControlledReturnRegistry, updates spawn/departure handling to consume and persist terminal return markers safely, introduces LocalRaidSpectatorController and deterministic spectator target selection, and wires new serialized spectator/cancel UI controls into RaidMenuView/Presenter. Inventory mutation entry points are now locally blocked while defeated. Includes new/updated edit mode and play mode tests plus architecture docs covering the new defeat/spectator and lifecycle rules.
```

### e728743d1a57624f43d7c30884669c3b7845a680

[e728743d1a57624f43d7c30884669c3b7845a680](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/e728743d1a57624f43d7c30884669c3b7845a680)

Date: 2026-08-12T02:49:04-03:00 · Classification: Other Changes (unknown) · Systems: Networking & Sessions, Persistence & Backend, Build & Tooling, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
Replace Town raid queue with preparation system
```

#### Original body

```text
Replace the legacy Town raid queue with a new Preparation system and expand raid capacity to 16. Introduces RaidLaunchContext, RaidSessionRules, RaidAdmissionRules, RaidParticipantSpawnRules and a set of TownRaidPreparation types (Directory, NetworkController, Snapshot, Rules, Index, Cache, Member, Presentation). Removes the old RaidLaunchManifest/Queue controllers and associated assets; updates FusionSessionLauncher, NetworkRunnerFactory, NetworkSpawnManager, HostMigration, Hub launchers/spawners and presenter/view code to use the new launch context and preparation APIs. Scenes/prefabs updated for 16 player spawn points. Adds many unit tests covering new rules and behaviors and adjusts build/profile settings.
```

### 13ed85a123906b1e3b0570bca795d6415bdf42b0

[13ed85a123906b1e3b0570bca795d6415bdf42b0](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/13ed85a123906b1e3b0570bca795d6415bdf42b0)

Date: 2026-08-11T18:35:50-03:00 · Classification: Features (inferred) · Systems: Networking & Sessions, UI, Build & Tooling, Documentation, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
Add host-return migration lifecycle and adoption
```

#### Original body

```text
Implements a host-return host-migration flow where a departing host can leave migration ownership to peers. Key changes:

- FusionSessionLauncher: new APIs (ShutdownForHostMigrationDeparture, TryBeginHostMigration, TryAdoptMigratedRunner, ReportHostMigrationFailure) and adoption logic.
- HostMigrationLifecycleController: create/start replacement runner, wait for snapshot+rebind completion before handing composition to launcher; stronger validation and cleanup.
- HostMigrationSnapshotRestorer: report failures to owner instead of forcing MainMenu.
- NetworkSpawnManager: one-shot HostMigration completion task, rebind tracking, timeout and completion semantics.
- SessionConnectionCoordinator/RaidMenuPresenter: participant-return path that may use host-migration departure and suppresses recovery on HostMigration.
- Tests added and docs updated.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
```

```text
Retain local HUD after participant defeat
```

#### Original body

```text
Refined HUD ownership to follow the local raid participant lifecycle: gameplay HUD now waits for participant/avatar resolution during raiding, but remains bound for the local participant’s terminal defeat result even after avatar authority/current-avatar links are cleared. Added one-shot terminal return request guarding in `RaidMenuPresenter` to prevent duplicate return intents and ensure return only after valid terminal conditions. Expanded PlayMode coverage for unresolved links, local vs remote ownership, and defeated-return flow, and updated architecture docs to match the new ownership and return behavior.
```

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
Coordinate host release in raid launch
```

#### Original body

```text
Reworks launch flow to delay host release until all non-host members have been released and observed as departed, with a configurable timeout that cancels launch if departures stall. Adds launch/departure transition logging, tracks expected/released/departed remote profiles, and resets this state on queue reset. Queue dissolve rules were also tightened so departures only dissolve the queue when the host leaves, preventing non-host launch departures from tearing down the queue.
```

#### Original subject

```text
Shift raid prep to Town cohort flow
```

#### Original body

```text
Moves player-facing raid creation/joining from direct coordinator calls into the replicated Town queue workflow, including authoritative raid-code generation, code-validated joins, ready/start actions, and snapshot/UI support for preparation state. Adds `RaidLaunchContext` to preserve frozen cohort identity across runner shutdown/startup, wires it into `RaidTransitionTicket`, and updates transition behavior so coordinated clients retry only transient `GameNotFound` availability (up to a fixed limit) while treating `GameClosed` as terminal. Architecture docs were updated to reflect the new Town-preparation-owned lifecycle and technical-only waiting phase in the raid runner.
```

### 0884c46fb444bbe15c8a833202d5c49e194bd7ad

[0884c46fb444bbe15c8a833202d5c49e194bd7ad](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/0884c46fb444bbe15c8a833202d5c49e194bd7ad)

Date: 2026-08-11T01:07:51-03:00 · Classification: Other Changes (unknown) · Systems: Combat, Movement, Inventory & Loot, Networking & Sessions, UI, Build & Tooling, Documentation, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
Gate raid start behind bootstrap flow
```

#### Original body

```text
Reworks coded raid startup so sessions stay in `WaitingForPlayers` until the host explicitly starts the raid. `NetworkMatchController` now uses `TryStartRaid()` to close admission, run a one-time initial PvPvE bootstrap via `NetworkSpawnManager`, and only then move to `InProgress`; bootstrap failures now trigger authoritative closure with `BootstrapFailure`.

Code-admission availability is narrowed to `WaitingForPlayers`, initial enemy/loot/breakable generation is deferred out of scene-load completion, and spawn helpers now return success/failure so bootstrap errors are surfaced deterministically. Player movement/combat/interaction/consumable/loot controllers are also phase-gated to block gameplay actions before `InProgress`. Related tests and architecture docs were updated to match the new waiting->starting->in-progress lifecycle.
```

```text
Switch to code-based raids and local profile state
```

```text
Reworks Town-to-raid flow around six-digit raid codes: the Town presenter/view now create or join coded sessions, manifests support code admission, and session startup/admission logic was updated to distinguish pending host availability from definitive failures. Local profile and stash lifetime is now process-scoped (new in-memory profile repository and non-persistent profile identity), with related coordinator/loadout handling updates. Visibility was tightened to local-avatar ownership via a new LocalPlayerVisibilityBinder, entity LOS checks now support collider-footprint sampling, loot pickups gained required NetworkTransform wiring, and tests/docs were updated to match the new behavior.
```

[eb16a1415dc493037cc4cc93e210bc9d31b549ac](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/eb16a1415dc493037cc4cc93e210bc9d31b549ac)

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
Enforce raid loadout reservations on admission
```

#### Original body

```text
Moves raid loadout ownership to coordinated admission data instead of prefab-time local injection. The coordinator now creates/rolls back/confirms durable loadout reservations, the admission token (v2) carries reservation+loadout with strict size/shape validation, and spawn authority initializes player inventory only from validated admission data. Also removes `PlayerLoadoutInjector` from network player prefabs, threads reservation IDs through participants/session factory, and updates tests/docs for reservation durability and admission guarantees.
```

Rewires bootstrap and stash/loadout services to act as adapters over `LocalProfileStore`, adds profile commit events for UI refreshes, and includes configuration assets plus edit-mode tests covering round-trip saves, backup recovery, schema rejection, and extraction idempotency. Also documents the architecture and durability/authority boundaries.

[0748702e73412954bd4bd02b8702ac9726ad9962](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/0748702e73412954bd4bd02b8702ac9726ad9962)

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
Add town raid queue and participant model
```

#### Original body

```text
Introduces a full Town-to-raid coordinated flow with manifest-based admission: new `TownRaidQueueNetworkController`/NPC interaction, `RaidLaunchManifest` + admission token codec, client launch retries, and private session admission windows. Splits persistent raid identity from combat avatars via `NetworkRaidParticipant` and `RaidAvatarParticipantLink`, updates spawning/host migration/restoration, and wires extraction/defeat/return state transitions through participant state. Also updates Social/Network prefabs and Town scene composition, adjusts interaction result delivery and local binders for authority-safe presentation, and adds focused EditMode/PlayMode tests plus architecture docs for the new systems.
```

### a8e85b4095d8ccb5213c6378c0440a0387c79878

[a8e85b4095d8ccb5213c6378c0440a0387c79878](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/a8e85b4095d8ccb5213c6378c0440a0387c79878)

Date: 2026-08-09T21:57:51-03:00 · Classification: Other Changes (unknown) · Systems: Abilities, Networking & Sessions, UI, Build & Tooling, Documentation, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
Town-Raid-Town session architecture
```

#### Original body

```text
SessionConnectionCoordinator: persistent owner of Town/Raid connections, transitions, recovery, and the development route.
SessionConnectionStateMachine: pure state machine for transition validation and concurrent-request rejection.
SessionConnectionState, SessionTransitionResult, RaidConnectionRole, RaidConnectionRequest, and RaidTransitionTicket: lifecycle and request contracts.
ISessionRunnerOwner and RunnerShutdownUtility: idempotent shutdown, effective runner destruction, and stale-callback protection.
LauncherShutdownListener: shutdown notifications and initial OnSceneLoadDone synchronization.
NetworkSceneBuildIndexResolver: safe scene resolution by name or path.
HubSessionLauncher and FusionSessionLauncher: explicit scenes, NetworkSceneManagerDefault, and initial scene-load synchronization.
HubPlayerSpawner and HubSpawnSceneConfiguration: Town-owned social spawning, order-independent callbacks, and SetPlayerObject.
SocialPlayerCharacter and SocialPlayer.prefab: social avatar without combat, damage, loot, extraction, corpse, raid HUD, or minimap components.
DirectRaidDevelopmentStarter: direct raid entry for development only.
MainMenuController and MainMenu Canvas: Create now enters Town as Enter Town; Join Room is hidden.
Systems.prefab, MainMenu.unity, and Lobby-Town.unity: persistent composition, camera, input, spawn, and scene configuration.
Removed HubSessionDebugStarter.
SessionCompositionConfigurationTests: EditMode validation for prefabs, scenes, composition, and raid-component exclusions.
Updated HubSessionLauncherTests to use the social prefab.
Rewrote [LobbyAndSessionTransitionArchitecture.md](/C:/Users/Dani/OneDrive/Documentos/GitHub/ProjectGrimhold/Project Grimhold/Docs/Architecture/LobbyAndSessionTransitionArchitecture.md).
```

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
implement entity visibility presentation infrastructure
```

#### Original body

```text
Added the core presentation infrastructure for LOS-based entity culling:
- `IVisibilityTarget`: The interface defining the visibility point and visual toggle.
- `EntityVisibilityPresenter`: A companion component to manage renderers without coupling gameplay code.
- `EntityVisibilitySystem`: A scene-level manager that evaluates all registered targets against the LosPolygonHandle in LateUpdate.
This sets up the system to selectively cull entities when they are outside the LOS polygon.
```

```text
and apply a smoothstep falloff. Expose _FalloffEnabled (toggle),

properties. Falloff is independent of _MaskBlurTexels. No LOS,
geometry or gameplay changes.
```

### 91a374aefffddb5ac60958b5966e2d73859268de

[91a374aefffddb5ac60958b5966e2d73859268de](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/91a374aefffddb5ac60958b5966e2d73859268de)

Date: 2026-08-07T23:58:09-03:00 · Classification: Features (inferred) · Systems: World & Visibility, Art & Animation

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
add configurable mask edge smoothing to FogOfWar shader
```

#### Original body

```text
Replace single-point mask sample with a 3x3 box filter. Add
_ProcessedMask to Properties block with [HideInInspector] so Unity
populates _ProcessedMask_TexelSize automatically. Expose _MaskBlurTexels
property (float, range [0,4]) on the FogOfWar material. UV step is
derived from _ProcessedMask_TexelSize so smoothing is
resolution-independent. Migrate _ProcessedMask declaration to
TEXTURE2D/SAMPLER macros for consistency with URP HLSL.
No geometry, LOS, gameplay or Falloff changes.
No other visibility components modified.
```

#### Original subject

```text
Harden host migration snapshot restore flow
```

#### Original body

```text
Reworked host migration restore to be object-aware and fail-safe: dynamic/scene snapshot rebuild now validates IDs, runner/scene ownership, applies targeted EntityId fixups, enforces match controller integrity, and rolls back spawned objects on failure. Added `HostMigrationRestoreUtility.IsRestoreSpawn()` and replaced broad `!Object.IsResume` guards across gameplay/networked components so only objects actively being restored skip fresh `Spawned()` initialization. Also tightened migration lifecycle/startup checks (scene ref add validation, awaited runner shutdown), prevented duplicate snapshot-restore result reports, improved sanctuary presenter validity checks (`IsInSimulation`), and updated architecture docs to reflect HM-03 behavior and constraints.
```


Runner composition now includes this restorer and wires `HostMigrationResume` to it. `NetworkSpawnManager` was extended with explicit host-migration restore states and coordination flags so scene-load readiness and snapshot-restore completion are synchronized before unblocking runtime rebind. Also updates multiple networked `Spawned()` initializers to skip default-state resets during resume (`!Object.IsResume`), preserving migrated state instead of overwriting it.

### bc3a7f6f2202f6f73f3c70a3669ac21a50a02ff0

[bc3a7f6f2202f6f73f3c70a3669ac21a50a02ff0](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/bc3a7f6f2202f6f73f3c70a3669ac21a50a02ff0)

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
implement authoritative inventory consumable system
```

#### Original body

```text
Implement an authoritative, data-driven consumable system for the raid inventory over Photon Fusion 2.1.

- Introduce `IConsumableEffect` and `HealthConsumableEffect` for static data-driven effects.
- Integrate `ConsumableDefinition` into `LootDefinition`.
- Add `IHealable` contract to `CharacterBase` to apply authoritative healing.
- Add `PlayerConsumableNetworkController` to process client intentions securely using RPC sequences and state authority validation.
- Add `LootConsumeContextActionProvider` to expose contextual actions in the UI and handle visual feedback upon server confirmation/rejection.
- Fix internal validation bugs with self-targeted `LootTransferRequest` extraction.

All changes adhere to the decoupled network architecture, restricting state mutation strictly to the State Authority.
```

#### Original subject

```text
Add sanctuary ritual state and zone gating
```

#### Original body

```text
Implements TASK-55 by making `ExtractionSanctuary` an authoritative interactable ritual endpoint co-located with `ExtractionZone` under one identity. Adds replicated ritual lifecycle (`ExtractionRitualState` + timer), ritual progress snapshots, and config-driven ritual duration validation. Extraction now requires both zone availability and sanctuary ownership with completed ritual, while zone availability cannot be turned off after completion. Updates registry sanctuary unregistration semantics for shared-capability cleanup, adjusts prefab/scene composition to embed zone+collider+prompt on sanctuary objects, and expands edit/play mode tests plus architecture docs to cover ritual flow, authorization, and cleanup ordering.
```

```text
Add extraction sanctuary assignment system
```

```text
Implements TASK-54 sanctuary assignment with new sanctuary/read interfaces, assignment result/failure contracts, deterministic selection policy, and a runner-local assignment service that reserves sanctuaries under host authority. Integrates the flow into progress completion, extends EntityRegistry with isolated reader/sanctuary capabilities, adds the ExtractionSanctuary network prefab plus four Gameplay scene instances, and updates edit/play mode tests and extraction architecture docs to cover the new behavior.
```

### b01d86d9ebd53aa9f8fa6191dbe08454e25ce487

[b01d86d9ebd53aa9f8fa6191dbe08454e25ce487](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/b01d86d9ebd53aa9f8fa6191dbe08454e25ce487)

Date: 2026-08-03T01:35:49-03:00 · Classification: Features (inferred) · Systems: Combat, Extraction, Inventory & Loot, UI, World & Visibility, Build & Tooling, Documentation, Tests

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
Add extraction quota progress and loot provenance
```

#### Original body

```text
Implements US-13 individual extraction progress end-to-end: new progress contracts, receiver/defeat-source capabilities, registry support, and authoritative contribution flow from fatal damage, first container open, loot transfers, and pickups. Adds PlayerExtractionProgressController, ExtractionProgressDefeatSource, progress rules/snapshots, and wires prefab/config rewards and quota values.

Separates extraction countdown and quota models by renaming the old countdown snapshot to ExtractionCountdownSnapshot, updates controller/HUD usage, and adds broad EditMode/PlayMode coverage for rules, registry behavior, prefab composition, and simulation scenarios.

Also introduces loot first-acquisition provenance in transactions and containers, tracks eligible quantities to prevent duplicate credit, and decouples economy from progress by adding SellValuePerUnit and switching inventory/HUD value calculations to sell value.
```

### 6e15b5fd384cd7b4097b75ddbdfedfc0b674151a

[6e15b5fd384cd7b4097b75ddbdfedfc0b674151a](https://github.com/Astro-Rift-Games/ProjectGrimhold/commit/6e15b5fd384cd7b4097b75ddbdfedfc0b674151a)

Date: 2026-08-01T01:44:47-03:00 · Classification: Other Changes (unknown) · Systems: Combat, Art & Animation

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
Animator-driven enemy attacks + animation listener
```

#### Original body

```text
Adds slime attack AnimationClips and SlimeAttackConfig, updates the Slime AnimatorController with an Attack state and IsAttacking/OnAttack parameters, and updates the NetworkEnemyMelee prefab to include gizmo & animation-listener components. Introduces EnemyAttackAnimationListener (invoked by Animation Events) and refactors EnemyCombatAIController to commit attacks (TryCommitAttack), store a pending AttackRequest, and expose ExecutePendingDamage which applies damage only on State Authority when called from the animation hit frame. Exposes TriggerAttack on IAnimatorController/CharacterAnimatorView, updates EnemyAnimatorView to drive IsAttacking, and suppresses procedural swings in EnemyCombatPresenter. Adds gizmo drawing support for melee attacks.
```

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
Use animator and colliders for defeat
```

#### Original body

```text
Refactor defeat presentation to rely on the Animator and colliders instead of procedural rotation/alpha transitions.

- DefeatPresenterBase: removed per-sprite/transform transition logic and related serialized fields; added Collider2D[] _colliders and SetCollidersEnabled to disable/enable hit detection on death; simplified TriggerDefeat and CancelAndRestore to notify animator and toggle colliders.
- EnemyDefeatPresenter / PlayerDefeatPresenter: minor attribute and documentation updates; removed overridden hiding behavior.
- Prefabs (NetworkEnemy, NetworkPlayer, NetworkEnemyMelee): updated references to use collider components and adjusted collider size/offsets/local positions.

Result: visual defeat animation is handled by the Animator Controller; corpses no longer use scripted rotation/fade but colliders are disabled on defeat.
```

Flags: primary or unclassified

#### Original subject

```text
Add EnemyFSM Idle state & Defeated animation
```

#### Original body

```text
Introduce Idle as the default enemy state and add defeated animation/animator integration. Renamed Player.controller -> Character.controller and added Defeated state, OnDefeated parameter and transition; created Defeated.anim. Updated prefabs (NetworkEnemy, NetworkEnemyMelee, NetworkEnemyRanged) to include/slot an EnemyFSM component. Code changes: EnemyPatrolState renamed to EnemyIdleState and enum value Patrol -> Idle; EnemyFSM now starts in Idle, adds proxy sync (Render/SyncProxyCurrentState) and registers Idle state; EnemyCharacter now holds and uses EnemyFSM to transition to Dead on death and validates FSM dependency; CharacterAnimatorView triggers OnDefeated; EnemyCombatAIController disables attack by default for state authority. Added architecture doc EnemyFSMArchitecture.md. Coherent network/state sync and prefab wiring updates included.
```
